messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Metoprolol crosses the placenta and passes into breast milk in small amounts.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
Studies published to date have not shown a link between metoprolol taken in pregnancy and major birth defects or miscarriage.
Reports on growth restriction, early birth, and death around the time of birth have been inconsistent.
Those studies have limitations that make studies hard to interpret.
Untreated high blood pressure and untreated heart failure in pregnancy carry their own serious risks for both mother and baby.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol may have low blood pressure, low blood sugar, a slow heartbeat, or slow breathing.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol are watched after birth.
The amount of metoprolol a breastfed baby receives is estimated at 0.05 mg to under 1 mg a day.
This amount is about 0.5% to 2% of the mother's weight-adjusted dose.
No side effects in breastfed babies have been identified.
Babies are still monitored for a slow heartbeat and for signs such as unusual sleepiness.
Triples: [["Metoprolol", "crosses placenta", "breast milk"], ["Metoprolol", "passes into", "breast milk"], ["Metoprolol", "has administration instruction", "tell doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding"], ["Metoprolol", "has study result", "no link to major birth defects or miscarriage"], ["Metoprolol", "has study result", "inconsistent reports on growth restriction, early birth, and death around birth"], ["Metoprolol", "has study limitation", "studies hard to interpret"], ["Untreated high blood pressure", "has risk", "serious risks for mother and baby"], ["Untreated heart failure", "has risk", "serious risks for mother and baby"], ["Metoprolol", "may cause in baby", "low blood pressure"], ["Metoprolol", "may cause in baby", "low blood sugar"], ["Metoprolol", "may cause in baby", "slow heartbeat"], ["Metoprolol", "may cause in baby", "slow breathing"], ["Metoprolol", "has post birth monitoring", "babies watched after birth"], ["Metoprolol", "has breastfed baby dose", "0.05 mg to under 1 mg a day"], ["Metoprolol", "has breastfed baby dose", "0.5% to 2% of mother's weight-adjusted dose"], ["Metoprolol", "has study result", "no side effects identified in breastfed babies"], ["Metoprolol", "has post birth monitoring", "monitor for slow heartbeat and unusual sleepiness"]]
Relations: ["crosses placenta", "has administration instruction", "has breastfed baby dose", "has post birth monitoring", "has risk", "has study limitation", "has study result", "may cause in baby", "passes into"]
Answer:

completion:
crosses placenta: The subject substance is able to pass through the placental barrier and reach the fetal circulation.
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the administration instruction specified by the object entity to be followed by patients.
has breastfed baby dose: The subject drug is received by the breastfed baby in the dose amount specified by the object entity.
has post birth monitoring: The subject drug requires the post-birth monitoring specified by the object entity to be performed on the baby.
has risk: The subject condition or factor is associated with the risk specified by the object entity for the affected individuals.
has study limitation: The subject study or findings are limited by the factors specified by the object entity, which affect the interpretation of the results.
has study result: The subject drug or condition is associated with the study result specified by the object entity based on current research.
may cause in baby: The subject drug may lead to the adverse effect or condition specified by the object entity in the baby.
passes into: The subject substance is transferred or transported into the entity specified by the object.
